{{Short description|Method to approximate a probability distribution}}

'''Expectation propagation (EP)''' is a technique in [[Bayesian inference|Bayesian machine learning]].<ref name="bishop">{{Cite book|title=Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning|last=Bishop|first=Christopher|publisher=Springer-Verlag New York Inc.|year=2007|isbn=978-0387310732|location=New York}}</ref>

EP finds approximations to a [[probability distribution]].<ref name="bishop" /> It uses an [[iterative]] approach that uses the factorization structure of the target distribution.<ref name="bishop" />  It differs from other Bayesian approximation approaches such as [[variational Bayesian methods]].<ref name="bishop" />

More specifically, suppose we wish to approximate an intractable probability distribution <math>p(\mathbf{x})</math> with a tractable distribution <math>q(\mathbf{x})</math>. Expectation propagation achieves this approximation by minimizing the [[Kullback–Leibler divergence]] <math>\mathrm{KL}(p||q)</math>.<ref name="bishop" /> Variational Bayesian methods minimize <math>\mathrm{KL}(q||p)</math> instead.<ref name="bishop" />

If <math>q(\mathbf{x})</math> is a Gaussian <math>\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{x}|\mu, \Sigma)</math>, then <math>\mathrm{KL}(p||q)</math> is minimized with <math>\mu</math> and <math>\Sigma</math> being equal to the [[mean]] of <math>p(\mathbf{x})</math> and the [[covariance]] of <math>p(\mathbf{x})</math>, respectively; this is called [[Method of moments (statistics)|moment matching]].<ref name="bishop" />

==Applications==
Expectation propagation via moment matching plays a vital role in approximation for [[indicator functions]] that appear when deriving the [[Belief propagation|message passing equations]] for [[TrueSkill]].
